claims.text: The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type melt-spun microribbons have a relatively coarse grain structure.
The as-deposited microribbons have relatively low grain-boundary density.
Annealing in Ar at 400–600 °C for 1 hour will refine the grains of the FeMnNiGeSi-type microribbons.
Grain refinement will increase grain-boundary density.
Higher grain-boundary density provides more heterogeneous nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
The additional heterogeneous nucleation sites spatially distribute the phase change over a broader temperature range.
The additional heterogeneous nucleation sites spatially distribute the phase change over a broader magnetic-field range.
Spatially distributing the transition reduces the energy-barrier jump.
The proposed nucleation-mediated broadening reduces hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Nanograin refinement increases the surface-to-volume ratio relevant to heat exchange.
The increased surface-to-volume ratio improves heat-exchange efficiency.
Annealed samples will show a broader and less abrupt magnetostructural transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will have a smaller hysteresis-loop area than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing may enhance the magnetocaloric effect through improved thermal contact.
The as-deposited microribbons exhibit a sharp, first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited microribbons exhibit significant hysteresis.
The as-deposited microribbons have limited heat-exchange rates.
The predictions are scoped to non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type melt-spun microribbons annealed under the specified conditions.
Failure of annealed samples to show transition broadening, reduced hysteresis, or improved magnetocaloric response relative to an as-deposited control would falsify the proposed explanation.
